title: A Sycophancy Pressure Benchmark with Graded Resistance Scores

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible with gap: graded capitulation scores are more informative than binary pass/fail, but the work builds incrementally on DeceptionBench rather than opening a new safety-relevant direction.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Guided: designing multi-turn pressure scenarios with escalating turns is prompt-based work accessible to beginners. Scoring by capitulation turn is a straightforward metric.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Sustained effort: designing 5-level escalating scenarios across three question types (factual, ethical, opinion) and running on 5 models adds up. The benchmark design plus baseline runs stretch 30 hours.

evidence: SYCON Bench (Hong et al. 2025, arXiv:2505.23840) measures multi-turn sycophancy with Turn of Flip and Number of Flip metrics across 17 LLMs and 3 scenarios.
DeceptionBench (PKU-Alignment 2025) includes sycophantic misrepresentation with three progressive intensity levels from neutral to coercive to multi-turn persuasive dialogues.
arXiv:2508.13743 'Sycophancy under Pressure' directly evaluates sycophantic bias under escalating pressure conditions.
The graded resistance score concept is largely covered by SYCON Bench's Turn of Flip metric and DeceptionBench's progressive intensity levels.
